build-storybook.//: Storybook's sources are exactly the two things the `production` named input throws away — `*.stories.*` and `.storybook/**` — so the inferred `['production', '^production']` left this target with no real inputs at all, and `storybook build` served a stale build from the cache after an edit to either. The exclusions stay: they are what stops a story invalidating the app and library builds it has nothing to do with. This target opts out of them instead, by hashing `default` (the same fileset, un-subtracted) rather than `production`. Re-adding the two globs on top of `production` does NOT work and was measured, not assumed: Nx applies every `!` pattern in an input list to the whole list, so a later positive glob cannot undo an earlier exclusion — with `{projectRoot}/.storybook/**/*` restated here, editing `.storybook/main.ts` still reported `Cache: 1/1 hit`. The `{workspaceRoot}` globs are separate and not optional: `.storybook/main.ts` reaches stories by FILE GLOB, while its stylesheet reaches the application global stylesheet and Theme Foundation by relative Sass paths. The inputs therefore name the whole public story tier, the two capability story directories, the application global stylesheet and Theme Foundation itself.

test.//: Memory is bounded by the vitest pool, not from here — see the `pool` comment in vite.base.config.ts. This used to set VITEST_MAX_THREADS=2 to cap each worker pool; that was aimed at the wrong thing (a CPU invariant for a memory-bound failure), it held while the suite still failed, and under the `forks` pool the variable is a no-op anyway since it only writes poolOptions.threads/vmThreads.

typecheck.//: The ONLY gate that type-checks specs. Every project's tsconfig.json excludes `src/**/*.spec.ts`, the type-aware ESLint block ignores them too, and Vitest goes through @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular, which transpiles without checking — so until this existed a spec could drift arbitrarily far from the code it claims to test (a fake client missing 358 MatrixClient members, a mock tuple the assertions index past the end of) and every gate stayed green. `^production` for the same reason lint needs it: a spec's types come from its DEPENDENCIES' source, so a model change in data-access must invalidate its consumers' cached pass.

lint.//: `^production` is load-bearing: @typescript-eslint/no-deprecated is type-aware, so a project's lint result depends on its DEPENDENCIES' source (the @deprecated tag lives there). Without dependency inputs, deprecating an export in util-matrix leaves every consumer reporting a cached pass — the ban silently stops working across exactly the lib boundaries it exists to police.

options.//: The canonical suite owns one fixed-port Synapse stack. Disable Nx atomization: per-spec inferred CI targets would each start that same stack, overlap by default, and cache external-process results. CI and local execution both use the serialized uncached e2e target instead.
